chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: God, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Whoever falls ill for three (days) and does not complain to any of his visitors, I will replace his flesh with flesh better than his, and blood better than his. If I then restore him to health, I restore him without any sin upon him; and if I take his soul, I take it to My mercy.'

key_terms.أَبْدَلْتُهُ: I replace/substitute for him — divine action of transformation, implying spiritual and physical renewal
key_terms.عُوَّادِهِ: His visitors/consolers who come to check on the sick person; 'iyada (visiting the sick) is a recommended act
key_terms.قَبَضْتُهُ إِلَى رَحْمَتِي: I take him to My mercy — death as a transition into God's mercy, not punishment

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about patient endurance during illness?
ai.summary: This is a hadith qudsi (a divine saying narrated by the Prophet) transmitted through Imam al-Baqir (AS). It presents a divine promise: a person who endures three days of illness without complaining to those who visit them will be spiritually purified — their body renewed with better flesh and blood. Whether they recover or die, God promises either a sinless return to health or a merciful death. The hadith encourages patient endurance (sabr) during illness and suggests that physical suffering, borne in silence, is a means of spiritual purification and divine favor.
word_analysis: I take his soul (cause him to die)

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Salim, from Ahmad Bin Al Nazar, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> having said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Said: “

The one who gets sick for three (days) and he does not complain to anyone from his consolers, I<sup>azwj</sup> would Change his flesh to better than his (current) flesh, and to better blood than his (current) blood. So if I<sup>azwj</sup> were to Grant him good health, it would be with no sins for him, and if I<sup>azwj</sup> were to Capture him (Cause him to die), would do so to My<sup>azwj</sup> Mercy”’.
en.sarwar: 1. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn Salim from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr from ‘Amr ibn Shamir from Jabir who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, says, “

If one remains ill for three days and does not complain about it to anyone of his visitors, I change his flesh into a better flesh and his blood into a better blood. If I give him good health, I give him a good health free from sin. If I take him (away) from this life, I take him into My mercy.’””
